column1: # Decisions on what the routing hook's keyword path admits (#310).
# Read by scripts/keyword-path-audit.sh, which measures every keyword in
# config/default-triggers.json through the real hook and fails when this file and the
# measurement disagree, in either direction. Regenerate the measurement with
# One row for every keyword measured `keyword-only` or `inert`. A `covered` keyword has
# class     keyword-only  the keyword admits the skill and no trigger does
#           inert         the keyword cannot fire: the hook skips a keyword under 6
#                         characters, and compares it as written against a lowercased
#                         prompt, so one holding a capital never matches
# decision  recall  wanted: the same request as a trigger, in wording a trigger lacks
#           gap     defeats a constraint a trigger or a fixture encodes; to be narrowed
#           open    could be either; the owner's call. Every inert row is open: delete
# One kind of keyword gets no class and so no row: one the hook does not score when it is
# the whole prompt (a greeting with a word or two after it, a leading slash) but which
# fires inside a longer one. The audit exits 3 on it; it has to be reworded or removed.
# The decision column records a judgement. Nothing checks it except that it is one of the
# three words; what is checked is that a row exists and its class is still true.
# Field evidence, 2026-10-08, one owner: 598 distinct typed prompts from transcripts that
# label a prompt's origin (2026-09-05 to 2026-10-07). 9 contained any keyword. Removing
# every keyword changed the selection on 2, both through `health check`: on one the
# keyword alone selected incident-analysis, on the other its 20 points decided which
# domain skill was kept. No other row below has a field observation for or against it.
